title: Refactor run_batch() to use asyncio.TaskGroup for parallel WU execution
description: Replace the sequential `for wu in batch` loop in run_batch() with asyncio.TaskGroup. Create merge_lock and state_lock as asyncio.Lock instances at the top of the function and pass them to every execute_wu() call. Collect verdicts into a dict keyed by wu_id using a closure or a shared results dict populated by each task coroutine. After the TaskGroup block closes (all tasks complete), iterate results to build the summary dict and print per-WU verdicts. Remove the per-iteration `needs_user_pivot` break — the orchestrator handles pivot detection after run_batch() returns. The summary dict shape {ready, passed, failed, reshaped} and the function's external signature are unchanged.
acceptance_criteria: run_batch() creates merge_lock = asyncio.Lock() and state_lock = asyncio.Lock() before the TaskGroup
All WUs in the batch are launched as tasks inside a single `async with asyncio.TaskGroup() as tg:` block
Each task receives merge_lock and state_lock
The sequential `for wu in batch` loop is removed
Verdicts are collected after the TaskGroup closes and used to compute the summary dict
The function returns the same {ready, passed, failed, reshaped} dict
No sibling task is cancelled when a WU sets needs_user_pivot
